_meta.method: original literal English gloss from the Sanskrit commentary; Sanskrit order preserved; no machine-translation prose

1.translation: Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever steadfast, worship You in this way, and those who worship the Imperishable, the Unmanifest—who among them are the best knowers of Yoga?

2.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Those who, placing their minds in Me, worship Me, ever steadfast, endowed with supreme faith, are considered by Me to be the most united with Yoga.

3.translation: But those who worship the Imperishable, the Indefinable, the Unmanifest, the All-pervading, the Inconceivable, the Unchanging, and the Eternal.
word_for_word: unchanging, abiding as the fixed reality

4.translation: Having fully restrained the whole group of senses, viewing all things with equal understanding, and delighting in the welfare of all beings, they reach Me alone.
word_for_word: delighting in the welfare of all beings

5.translation: But greater is the difficulty for those whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest, for the path concerning the Unmanifest is attained with pain by embodied beings. Śrīdhara explains that constant inward turning is difficult for those identified with the body.
word_for_word: whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest

6.translation: But those who, dedicating all actions to Me, regard Me as supreme, and meditate on Me and worship Me through undivided Yoga alone—

7.translation: For those whose minds are fixed in Me, I become their deliverer from the ocean of mortality and worldly existence, and I do so without delay, O Pārtha.
word_for_word: from the ocean of mortality and worldly existence
for those whose minds are fixed in Me

8.translation: Fix your mind in Me alone; place your understanding in Me. Then you will dwell in Me alone hereafter—there is no doubt. Śrīdhara explains “hereafter” as after the end of the body, when knowledge obtained by My grace has matured.

9.translation: If you are unable to fix your mind steadily in Me, then seek to reach Me through the Yoga of practice, repeatedly withdrawing the distracted mind and remembering Me, O Dhanañjaya.

10.translation: If you are unable even to practice, become devoted to action for My sake. Performing actions for My sake, you will attain perfection.
word_for_word: be devoted to action for My sake

11.translation: If you are unable even to do this, then, taking refuge in My Yoga and mastering yourself, relinquish the fruits of all actions. Śrīdhara explains this as doing duties as far as possible by the Lord’s command, placing their seen and unseen results in His care, and giving up attachment to those results.
word_for_word: renunciation of the fruits of all actions

12.translation: Knowledge is indeed better than practice without right understanding; meditation is superior to knowledge; and renunciation of the fruits of action is superior to meditation. From renunciation, peace follows immediately.
word_for_word: renunciation of the fruits of action

13.translation: One who has no hatred toward any being, is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, equal in pleasure and pain, and forgiving—

14.translation: One who is ever content, a disciplined yogin, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding dedicated to Me—such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
word_for_word: with mind and understanding dedicated to Me
that one is dear to Me

15.translation: One from whom the world does not become disturbed, and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from elation, intolerance, fear, and agitation—that one is dear to Me.
word_for_word: elation at gaining what is desired
that one is dear to Me

16.translation: One who is without expectation, pure, capable, indifferent, free from distress, and one who has renounced all undertakings—such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me. Śrīdhara explains “without expectation” as free from longing even when something arrives unasked, and “indifferent” as free from partiality.
word_for_word: one who has renounced all undertakings
that one is dear to Me

17.translation: One who neither rejoices on obtaining what is pleasant, nor hates what is unpleasant, nor grieves over the loss of what is desired, nor longs for what has not been obtained, and who renounces good and evil—such a devoted person is dear to Me.
word_for_word: one who renounces good and evil
that one is dear to Me

18.translation: One who is equal toward enemy and friend, and likewise toward honor and dishonor, equal in cold and heat and in pleasure and pain, and free from attachment.

19.translation: One who is equal toward blame and praise, silent and restrained in speech, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in understanding, and devoted—such a person is dear to Me.

20.translation: But those devotees who, endowed with faith, regard Me as supreme and practice this dharma-nectar exactly as taught are exceedingly dear to Me. Śrīdhara calls it dharma-amṛta because it is a discipline that leads to immortality.
